html:
Thăng Long, meaning "ascending dragon", was the capital of Vietnam founded in 1010 by Lý Thái Tổ, the first king of the Lý dynasty. It is today's Hanoi.

Lý Thái Tổ moved the court from Hoa Lư, a fortress among limestone hills, to the open plain of the Red River, a better seat for ruling the delta. His edict on moving the capital is a famous text in Vietnamese history, and legend says he saw a golden dragon rise over the site. The citadel was begun in 1010 and finished the next year.

For most of the next eight centuries Thăng Long was the capital of Đại Việt. The Lý built the Temple of Literature there in 1070. The city survived Mongol raids in the 1200s and Ming occupation in the 1400s. When the Nguyễn dynasty moved the capital to Huế in 1802, its importance fell, and in 1831 it was renamed Hà Nội. Excavations since 2002 have uncovered layers of the old palaces, and the citadel was listed as World Heritage in 2010, the city's thousandth year.
sum: Thăng Long, meaning "ascending dragon", was the capital of Vietnam founded in 1010 by Lý Thái Tổ, the first king of the Lý dynasty. It is today's Hanoi.
